- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 3–7 days post-peak.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model may misalign with trend; adjust forecast to align with sentiment midpoint or average of last 3 sentiment values.
